# How far a word reaches cheat sheet {#word-reach-cheat-sheet}

A quick look at [how far a word reaches](/word-reach). Nothing here is new: each row links to the section that teaches it. Stage: **B** Beginner, **I** Intermediate, **A** Advanced.

## Which word covers which {#covers}

When two words both reach the whole clause, the earlier one covers the later one ([earlier covers later](/word-reach#earlier-covers-later)). The first row lists the words that follow text order. The rows after it are rules of their own: check them first, and fall back on text order only when neither word has one.

## What gets into a box {#boxes}

A box keeps words apart from the sentence around it: a clause in a join, a dependent, an island, a quote, or an aside ([what gets into a box](/word-reach#boxes)). Most columns name something from outside the box, and **yes** means it reaches in. The two columns about your frame run the other way: **yes** means a channel or a new frame inside the box starts or ends your frame. A dash means no page states it yet.

## What carries past a period {#past-the-period}

Most words stop at the period ([what carries past a period](/word-reach#past-the-period)). The things below carry on into later sentences, each until one of the events under **Ends with**. **Speakers** says whether each speaker keeps their own or both share one.
